title: Quality Studio run persistence
summary: Decision-ready storage design for durable Quality Studio review runs. The recommendation keeps the tested, Git-ignored .quality/runs recovery journal and adds a tracked folder-per-run archive under .quality/run-history. It preserves run plans, immutable stopped attempts, operation results, finding observations, typed verdicts and timestamps; extends the existing token ledger with operation IDs; defines deterministic history and two-run diff APIs; and supplies five implementation slices with acceptance criteria and a non-fabricating migration path. Build state 2026-09-06: the tracked .quality/run-history archive was never built; the unused ReviewRunArchive class was deleted and the dossier records that RP-1 to RP-5 remain unimplemented. Journal retention and non-resurrecting recovery shipped in its place. Implementation state 2026-09-07 (QS-85): the card's goal is met by other means and RP-1 to RP-5 stay unimplemented. Durable records survive restart via the .quality/runs journal and RecoverRuns, findings and token ledger are Git-tracked under .quality/reports/runs and .quality/usage, and the run history list, trend and two-run compare ship in frontend/src/app/run-history. A complete QS-85 implementation of RP-1 to RP-5 was rebased onto main, found to duplicate all of that, and was not integrated; it is preserved on backup/QS-85-salvage-2d240de. What the archive would still add - immutable per-attempt records, ledger-joinable operation rows, and history outliving the 50-run retention floor - is now a fresh product decision rather than a merge.
